problem: Prior semantic map completion methods either use high-dimensional discrete codebooks that inflate memory (SGM, 1.52 GB) or iterative diffusion/flow sampling that is too slow for real-time robot use. CNN/GNN completion methods are weak at localizing hidden target objects.
motivation: Reasoning about unobserved regions of top-down semantic maps can cut exploration in ObjectNav, but the module must be light and fast on resource-constrained robots. Semantic maps are one-hot/binary and sparse, so dense codebooks are a poor fit, which motivates bitwise tokens.
key_idea: Encode one-hot semantic maps into lookup-free bitwise tokens with a BitVAE and complete missing tokens with a single-pass BERT/MAE-style masked transformer trained with target-category (object-aware) masking and a learnable category embedding.
insight: Bitwise tokens match the binary structure of semantic maps and give lower FID than VQ codebooks (BitVAE 10 bits 1.65 vs VQVAE 1.70-1.75) with a smaller model. The largest gain comes from object-aware masking: BitVAE-9 goes from sSR 6.04 (random masking) to 45.84 (object-aware), with mIoU 30.43 to 34.10. Scaling the transformer from ViT-B to ViT-L doesn't help.
method: BitVAE tokenizer: patch CNN encoder (stride 16, 224x224 map -> 14x14 grid) outputs b=9 bits per token binarized by sign; residual CNN decoder reconstructs the map; trained with BCE + map IoU loss (weights 1.0 each).

Mask Transformer: ViT-B (12 layers, 12 heads, dim 768) with bidirectional attention predicts indices of unobserved tokens (vocab 2^b+1 including mask token) in one forward pass, using cross-entropy on masked positions.
Masking schedule: mask ratio starts at 15-20% for the first quarter of training then rises to 75% by cosine schedule.

Object-aware masking: in addition to random patch masking, all patches of a chosen goal category are masked and a learnable category embedding (n x d) is concatenated to the input tokens, teaching a prior over target locations at no extra inference cost.
ObjectNav integration: FastMap replaces the MAE-based generator in the SGM stack, keeping the frontier planner, RGB-D + semantic segmentation sensing and Gibson splits unchanged.
Unconditional variant (w.o. ObMask): random masking without a category token, used as a fair comparison against unconditional baselines.

setting.backbone: BitVAE (patch CNN encoder + residual CNN decoder) + ViT-B mask transformer, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Gibson ground-truth semantic maps (15 goal categories + room-layout channel), random crops/rotations following SGM; no extra data
setting.observation: partial top-down semantic map (224x224, 1 room-layout + 15 object channels) aggregated from RGB-D with semantic segmentation
setting.action_space: frontier-based planner in the SGM stack, with the completed map guiding goal selection
setting.privileged: Goal category given by ObjectNav spec; for map-generation eval the target category is masked out of the GT map (controlled protocol); semantic segmentation from simulator

results: FastMap reaches 34.10% mIoU and 45.84% sSR on Gibson, more than doubling SGM's 21.88% sSR, at 0.011 s/map with a 0.41 GB model (3.7x smaller than SGM's 1.52 GB). In ObjectNav it gets the highest SR (83.8%), beating GOAL (83.5) and NaviFormer (82.6), with SPL 43.7 (GOAL 44.2 is higher) and DTS 0.94 (NaviFormer 0.76 is lower).
limitations: Evaluated only on Gibson in simulation; no MP3D/HM3D and no real robot.
No robustness study for perception noise, odometry drift or map misalignment.
sSR is a lenient binary metric that favors target-conditioned methods, and navigation comparison to other systems is not strictly controlled.
